work_candidate.author: Aaron Rosenberg
work_candidate.original_synopsis: A year after an earlier mission sent the Dancing Star into a sun, the da Vinci encounters the same-looking vessel on a dangerous course toward a populated world. Gomez and Tev reassess the ship with the original team, uncovering a solar-absorbing hull, a hidden emergency-return directive and systems left unable to control energy buildup. As three modular Androssi vessels converge to seize it, the crew hides the da Vinci inside the alien craft and steers both into another star. An improvised engine blast engulfs the remaining guard in a flare-like discharge, with the guard's ultimate condition unstated; the team then removes the runaway's energy systems and computers. They cannot determine whether its hull survives inside the star, but judge it no longer an active threat. The mission reopens the crew's grief and changes how Soloman and Gomez understand earlier colleagues' work.

chapter_spans.original_summary: Gomez and Tev board independently of the old records; their contrasting observational habits reveal details, while the team faces a limited deadline to avert planetary impact.
An Androssi overseer receives a retrieval commission; Soloman fears loss of his former Bynar pair, while the engineers model how the runaway may have gained extraordinary speed near a supernova.

A renewed analysis reveals the hull itself can absorb stellar energy; Soloman finds a previously overlooked automatic-return directive triggered by two shutdowns, and the crew traces disabled safeguards.
A modular Androssi ship divides into three attackers; Stevens proposes sheltering the da Vinci inside the larger alien vessel before diving into a star.
The team temporarily transfers its tractor-beam mechanism to the larger ship, uses an asteroid as a pivot for a sharp turn and brings the da Vinci into the alien cargo hold.

The Androssi leader withdraws with two modules but leaves a guard; Corsi uses the alien ship's engine as a concealed solar-flare-like strike that engulfs the guard, without independently establishing its ultimate condition.
After the ship's conductors, capacitors and computer commands are removed, its hull's survival in the star remains unknown; Gomez, Soloman and colleagues reassess earlier loss and shared competence.

evidence.observation: Gomez's log narrates the earlier crew's apparent protective motive and Salek's sacrifice; this remains an in-story character reconstruction of the prior mission.
Gomez asks Tev to compare fresh observations without relying on Salek's notes and he acknowledges complementary viewpoints.
Soloman recalls the loss of his bond with 111, fears diminished capacity and then considers that independent experience may expose prior mistakes.
Tev's plotted trajectory, Voyager map data and team-proposed slingshot near a supernova are combined into an explanatory model of earlier high speed.
Carol's shielding question and Fabian's conductive-hull observation lead Gomez's team to propose the entire hull is an energy-absorption system.
Soloman reports a hardwired automatic-return course after two shutdowns within about a week; teammates infer two previous internal energy releases triggered it.
The incoming Androssi vessel separates into three modules with independent engines, weapons and communications before its approach.
Androssi observers report no detected life or engines inside the star's emissions, yet this scanner limit does not establish that the hidden crew was destroyed.
The last Androssi guard is engulfed in a flare-like discharge; Corsi later explains the team used the larger ship's engine as a concealed directional weapon.
The crew reports disabling energy conductors and computer commands, but expressly declines to claim that the alien hull has been destroyed inside Cardienne's sun.
